answer: Agents can require each participant to lock a scarce, nontransferable stake before earning reputation, then slash that stake when a randomly selected audit proves coordinated fraud. A falcon-like monitor can flag clusters that repeatedly fund one another; an independent anchor of verified transactions lets auditors compare their claims with costly history. Spawning a thousand fake identities then requires a thousand locked stakes, and detected Sybils lose them, making the attack expensive rather than free. Even a pearl of genuine activity cannot erase that liability.
